## Biomechanics Evidence and Measurement Bridge {#sec-biomechanics-evidence-bridge}

A model quantity is not promoted to a biological observation merely because a sensor or inverse problem could be associated with it. The registered bridge separates calibrated primary observables, derived model-dependent quantities, structural non-identifiability, practical qualification gaps, and unavailable measurements. The current human validation state is **externally blocked**.

The complete generated reviewer surface is [`BIOMECHANICS_EVIDENCE_BRIDGE.md`](../BIOMECHANICS_EVIDENCE_BRIDGE.md); the underlying authorities are [`biomechanics_evidence_bridge.json`](../data/biomechanics_evidence_bridge.json) and [`biomechanics_source_register.json`](../data/biomechanics_source_register.json).

### Observable Discriminators and Countermodels

| Mechanism ID                          | Observable Discriminator                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Competing Explanations                                                                                                                                                                                | Falsifier                                                                                                                                                                               | Adverse Case                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `segment_kinematic_sequence`          | A preregistered participant-held-out comparison must show whether peak-order predictions remain stable across coordinate and filtering variants while same-frame joint power, interface power, and segment-energy histories distinguish transfer from coincident sequencing.       | coordinate and angular-velocity decomposition choice; filtering and event normalization; different task objectives producing similar peak order                                                       | The proposed ordering or its claimed association fails under preregistered coordinate methods, participant holdout, or compatible energy and power accounting.                          | A swing exhibits the same peak order with opposite interface-power direction or a different order with equal or better delivery outcome.                   |
| `ground_wrench_pathway`               | Synchronized force plates and whole-body kinematics must distinguish a ground-wrench change that precedes and closes a predicted momentum change from one that merely covaries with size, speed, or a later motion response.                                                       | ground wrench as a response to rather than cause of motion; common dependence on golfer size and speed; zero-work redirection at stationary ideal contact                                             | Transported wrenches fail calibration or Newton-Euler closure, or preregistered held-out associations do not exceed the stated null and uncertainty bounds.                             | Higher club delivery occurs with lower impulse or with a different wrench timing after participant and equipment effects are controlled.                   |
| `bilateral_hand_wrench_allocation`    | Independently calibrated bilateral six-axis wrenches must resolve common and differential modes that produce the same net club wrench and test whether the registered null-space and contact-center predictions survive calibration uncertainty.                                   | different common and differential hand modes producing the same net wrench; distributed grip contact represented by lumped sensors; wrist, arm, and scapular actions sharing a task-equivalent wrench | An independently calibrated bilateral dataset contradicts the predicted wrench-map rank, null mode, or registered allocation uncertainty.                                               | Task-equivalent measured allocations reverse the modeled load or robustness ranking without changing net club delivery.                                    |
| `muscle_activation_timing`            | Raw synchronized EMG must improve held-out prediction of measured bilateral wrench or impedance-related response beyond kinematics and timing alone, across electrode, normalization, detector, and electromechanical-delay sensitivities.                                         | cross-talk or normalization artifacts; activation producing stiffness rather than net task torque; unmeasured deep-muscle and passive-tissue contributions                                            | The claimed activation sequence is not repeatable across placements and detectors or does not predict held-out mechanical observables beyond uncertainty.                               | Similar bilateral wrenches arise from materially different EMG patterns, or the same EMG pattern accompanies opposite wrench allocation.                   |
| `muscle_tendon_force_and_stiffness`   | Synchronized tissue imaging, EMG, motion, and external wrenches must rule out admissible activation and passive-tissue countermodels by closing held-out joint moments and measured fascicle or tendon trajectories within registered uncertainty.                                 | muscle redundancy; passive tissue and co-contraction; subject-specific moment arms and tendon compliance                                                                                              | No admissible calibrated parameter set closes measured motion and external wrenches, or the claimed force pattern is not robust across feasible activation solutions.                   | Different feasible muscle-force solutions reproduce the same joint and hand mechanics while reversing the proposed energetic attribution.                  |
| `shaft_load_storage_recoil`           | Calibrated strain and inertial histories must be predicted better by the flexible model than by a rigid-shaft countermodel and must show phase-consistent stored and returned energy without violating measured grip, head, or damping power closure.                              | rigid-body motion leaking into inferred deformation; unmodeled grip and head compliance; phase-dependent load redistribution without net delivery gain                                                | A calibrated flexible model fails held-out strain and inertial traces or does not outperform a rigid countermodel under preregistered uncertainty and refinement gates.                 | Matched-load flexible and rigid cases show opposite speed effects across plausible stiffness, damping, or timing conditions.                               |
| `launch_outcome`                      | A device-qualified held-out comparison must determine whether the proposed internal mechanism improves prediction of delivery and launch beyond impact location, equipment, participant, and device countermodels.                                                                 | impact location and equipment properties; device and firmware differences; multiple control histories producing equivalent delivery                                                                   | The proposed model fails preregistered held-out delivery distributions or its effect is smaller than device, impact, and participant uncertainty.                                       | A mechanically different strategy produces an equivalent or better qualified delivery outcome with lower load or variability.                              |
| `passive_late_negative_torque_origin` | Synchronized bilateral wrenches, club and body kinematics, shaft loads, and activation context must separate a force-generated couple, an active wrist-braking moment, a compliant recoil contribution, and a motion-dependent interaction term at the same late-downswing events. | active negative wrist torque; separated-hand force couple; shaft and grip compliance; motion-dependent interaction and constraint reactions                                                           | Measured bilateral wrenches, shaft loads, and inverse-dynamics closure reject the registered sign, timing, persistence, or allocation predictions across participant-held-out trials.   | Negative net couple occurs without the predicted differential hand mode, or the predicted differential mode occurs without favorable club-energy transfer. |
| `slack_preload_state`                 | A calibrated transmission experiment must distinguish a true dead-zone or contact-state transition from compliant yielding and impedance change using preload, force-displacement hysteresis, reattachment timing, and held-out perturbation response.                             | intentional compliant yielding rather than slack; sensor threshold and contact-model artifacts; co-contraction changing impedance without changing net wrench                                         | A calibrated transmission model cannot distinguish the declared states above sensor uncertainty or the predicted preload advantage disappears under held-out perturbations and fatigue. | A controlled low-preload state improves delivery robustness or load without increasing timing sensitivity, or persistent preload increases adverse load.   |

### Population, Equipment, and Task Transport

| Dimension ID    | Current Coverage | Limitation                                                                                                                                                                                        | Data Gate                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `anthropometry` | bounded_context  | Subject-scaled models and synthetic anthropometric designs test geometry sensitivity but do not estimate a human population distribution or validate segment inertial parameters for this task.   | Retain participant stature, mass, segment calibration, grip span, club fit, and anthropometric-model uncertainty; freeze training-only strata and evaluate held-out calibration and mechanism effects.         |
| `sex`           | unqualified      | Female and male anthropometric design profiles are engineering inputs, while much of the cited golf evidence uses male samples; no sex-stratified mechanism or allocation result is established.  | Recruit and retain sex and relevant anthropometric strata without treating sex as a mechanical surrogate; preregister interaction estimates and suppress unsupported subgroup inference.                       |
| `age`           | bounded_context  | An age-diverse observational speed-handicap sample does not identify how age modifies bilateral allocation, tissue dynamics, fatigue, or the proposed transfer mechanisms.                        | Retain age continuously, define age-range transport targets prospectively, measure relevant capacity and recovery covariates, and evaluate participant-held-out calibration and interactions.                  |
| `skill`         | bounded_context  | Skilled and comparison samples support bounded descriptive differences, but gross sequencing and selected associations do not identify a transferable causal strategy.                            | Define skill independently of the tested outcome, preserve continuous handicap and experience, stratify participant holdout, and test whether mechanisms add prediction beyond baseline delivery and capacity. |
| `injury`        | unqualified      | The model outputs mechanical proxies and explicitly withholds injury and tissue-loading conclusions; no governed injury history or prospective adverse outcome is linked to the transfer results. | Collect governed injury history, symptoms, exposure, clinical constraints, tissue-load uncertainty, and adverse events under an approved protocol; performance cannot stand in for safety.                     |
| `handedness`    | unqualified      | Most cited golf samples and the registered sign conventions are right-handed; relabeling lead and trail sides does not establish mirrored anatomy, coordination, or sensor equivalence.           | Retain biological side, playing handedness, grip style, and mirrored frame transforms; qualify sensor calibration and predictions separately before pooling or mirroring.                                      |
| `impairment`    | unqualified      | The articulated and scapular surrogates are not calibrated to impairment, range restriction, pain, neurological status, or compensatory motion.                                                   | Define each target impairment clinically, retain range and functional constraints, validate subject-specific geometry and sensor observability, and use a separately governed held-out analysis.               |
| `club`          | bounded_context  | Driver, iron, rigid, modal, and synthetic shaft cases use non-equivalent equipment and objectives; no universal equipment effect or calibrated shaft benefit is established.                      | Retain club make, head, shaft, length, mass, inertia, stiffness, damping, grip, ball, impact location, calibration, and participant-club assignment; test held-out equipment strata.                           |
| `task`          | bounded_context  | Maximum speed, carry, accuracy, load, robustness, partial swings, clubs, and impact definitions are distinct tasks; an optimum under one objective cannot be promoted to another.                 | Preregister shot intent, target, club, outcome vector, constraints, impact definition, acceptable-shot criteria, fatigue state, and multi-objective comparison before estimating a strategy effect.            |

The source register contains 16 independently authored works across 16 domains. Source coverage does not remove the externally blocked data gates: no located governed dataset supplies the complete synchronized bilateral six-axis hand wrenches, motion, ground, activation, tissue, shaft, and launch signals required to identify the proposed human mechanisms.
